MILE 12 WARRIOR | Business & Search Op: Read this before the keyword tabs. Target market: United States.

column2: Mile 12 Warrior is a driver-owned safety, fatigue and wellness resource brand for professional truck drivers, built on 25+ years of real driving experience (school bus, P&D, regional OTR). Not a carrier, not a recruiter, not a product company. The trust position is 'a driver talking to drivers'.

7-phase Driver Safety Roadmap; free tiered packets (New Driver + 90-Day Course with certificate, Seasoned Driver); two free Fleet Safety Department packets with DQ-file sign-off sheets; printable checklists; blog; forum ('Truckers Lounge'); shop; newsletter; and Social Butterflies for drivers' families.
(1) Professional drivers nationwide — new and 2+ year veterans. (2) Fleet safety directors who distribute packets at onboarding and annual refreshers. (3) Families and friends of drivers.
Shop, bookings/services (speaking, training, consulting), the Advertise page, fleet relationships, future course/packet upsells. Content is the top of every one of these funnels.

This is an informational-intent property. Commercial volume is small; the traffic engine is driver-problem and question search. Revenue keywords live almost entirely in the Fleet/B2B cluster. Strategy: win the informational SERP at scale, capture email, convert fleets on the B2B pages.

25+ years of verifiable lived experience. Google's E-E-A-T and every AI answer engine now weight first-hand experience heavily in YMYL-adjacent health and safety content. Almost no competitor in this vertical has it. It is currently under-signalled on the site.

Nearly all content sits on the homepage as scrolling phases rather than as individual indexable pages. One page cannot rank for 70 primary keywords. The single highest-impact fix is splitting the roadmap into discrete, schema-marked pages.
Free forum and gated packets can create thin or duplicate index bloat if login walls, print views and PDF versions are crawled. Needs canonical and robots discipline from day one.

Trucking is an unusually weak vertical for structured answers. Competitors run almost no FAQPage, HowTo or ItemList schema and none have llms.txt. Answer-first pages with proper markup should earn ChatGPT, Perplexity and AI Overview citations quickly.
70 primary keywords, each with 6 versions (2 Secondary, 2 LSI, 2 Question/Long-tail) = 490 total. Mapped across 13 clusters and 38 pages. Every keyword unique.

Phase 1 takes the winnable Tier 1 and Tier 2 primaries where competition is dated, thin or institutional. Head compliance terms (Tier 3) are pursued for AI citation and topical completeness, not for a #1 organic position against FMCSA.
